properties.description:
DELIVERED 2026-09-30 (chg:the-served-text-keeps-the-readers-lens-out-of-the-design), for req:a-design-holds-who-contributed-never-a-readers-persona, accepted 2026-09-28 with no capability and no check, which is why its clause "reflow2's served text says this, rather than telling the agent to record a background in the design" went two days unmet (fact:the-served-lens-still-tells-the-agent-to-record-a-readers-background-in-the-design-2026-09-30, live design).

WHAT EVERY SERVED TEXT NOW SAYS: a design holds who contributed to it (who wrote, who approved and, where it matters, their role on this design) and never a reader's persona. Applying the lens is the agent's job, and the lens comes from its host (a host such as flo2 hands over the signed-in person's persona with the design) or, with no host, from the agent's own memory of the person. With neither, the agent follows the person's own words and may ask once what they do day to day and what they trained in, keeping the answer out of the design.

WHERE: the lens on list_skills, get_skill and loop_status (skills.rs lens_line; its empty case now opens "THIS DESIGN DOES NOT SAY WHO IS READING, AND IS NOT MEANT TO", and its described case lists contributors for attribution and their role, never as the reader's lens); where-am-i's "Who you are talking to" step (the ask survives, host first, then memory, then the person's words; the answer stays out of the design); the served instructions' "Find out whose domain it is"; topic, why and detect-and-ask; and add_contributor's `description` parameter, which now says attribution and role, not a reader's persona.

WHAT STAYS OWED ELSEWHERE: req:the-agent-learns-who-it-is-talking-to and req:the-agent-says-which-recorded-reader-it-assumes-and-the-lens-names-them keep their "TO BE REVISED" notes, which wait for @ajs's word; the backgrounds already written into who:ajs and who:alex are untouched. The check proves the text is stated; it does not prove an agent acts on it.
properties.name: reflow2's served text tells the agent to apply the reader's lens without writing it into the design
